content.comment_body: I tested with my [product_name] [version_no] as Modbus client and an EATON easyE4 as Modbus server. Communication still fails. Testing with my other [product_name] [version_no] works without issues. It appears that the [product_name] [version_no] has trouble establishing Modbus connections.
Please share the solution here if one becomes available.
A factory reset did not solve the issue.

Yes, I received a reply, but nothing helpful so far. They advised further investigation using a managed switch, port forwarding, and capturing communication traces between [product_name] and PAC2200 for analysis. However, Support has not yet provided a definitive solution, and I haven't had time for these steps yet. Ideally, Support should handle this analysis, especially since they confirmed the configuration is correct.

Support has not provided a solution for the [product_name] [version_no] as client and EATON easyE4 as server via Modbus. However, the Modbus connection works if EATON easyE4 is the client and [product_name] [version_no] is the server. Recently, support suggested that the increased performance of [product_name] [version_no] may be causing issues for the EATON easyE4. Since the same project worked with [product_name] [version_no] as client, I believe [product_name] [version_no] is the source of the problem.

I reached the same conclusion. For this project, I also use a 4G gateway as the modbus client and [product_name] as the server, and everything works well for me. I accept the performance increase, but it's disappointing if two components from the same company lose compatibility. Given that the same configuration works with the previous version, it’s clear the newer version is the issue.

As promised, here is the fix provided by [company_name]. In the Modbus connection page of [product_name] software, PAC2200 was set to unit ID 255 by default. For unknown reasons, [product_name] sets the ID to 0 during communication instead of 255. I changed the unit ID to 5, and it’s now functioning correctly.

I resolved the issue with [product_name] [version_no] as client with EATON easyE4 as server by changing the Unit-ID in the connection table from 255 to 1. It works now. Thank you again for your feedback.
Did this solution work for you too? Maybe we can consider it a universal workaround.

As mentioned earlier, this feels like a workaround rather than a real solution. The true fix would be if [company_name] corrected the bug through a firmware update or software revision. It's unclear where the error lies—in the firmware or in the software—only the developers can address and resolve this.
I agree completely. This is also how [company_name] Support described the situation.
We'll have to wait and see when or if a proper bug fix is released. In my case, I've had no updates from Support for a week.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered problems with Modbus communication when using [product_name] [version_no] as a client, while prior versions worked without issue. Efforts such as factory resets and following support instructions have not resolved the problem. The performance improvements in the newer version may have introduced incompatibility with some third-party devices. Users express frustration with the lack of effective support or thorough investigation from [company_name].
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] [version_no] to communicate reliably via Modbus, maintaining compatibility just as previous versions did. They hope for more effective support from [company_name], including updates that will not compromise integration with standard protocols or existing systems.
